items.headline: Sensex adds 308 points to 74,459.53; Nifty reclaims 23,000 but midcaps and smallcaps fall up to 2%
items.summary: IT and pharma led; pharma gained about 7% over the week. Nifty rose nearly 2% on the week after last week's losses. Second straight up day; broad market weak.
items.rationale: A stronger rupee, the Fed pause and earnings support large caps, while high crude weighs on smaller, more domestic companies.

items.headline: Brent's expiring December contract settles about 2.4% higher at $117.64, highest since April
items.summary: A fourth straight monthly gain, estimated at 11–15%, after a tanker was hit by explosives near Hormuz. Reverses Friday's earlier dip. Escalating.
items.rationale: Crude near $118 raises India's import bill and fuel subsidy risk, feeds inflation and keeps pressure on the rupee and bonds.

items.headline: Tanker with 27 Indians hit by limpet mines near Hormuz; a second ship attacked, all Indian crew safe
items.summary: Explosives attached by a small boat started an engine-room fire 25 nautical miles from Khasab. Iran says tankers on unauthorised routes caught fire. Escalation of record October attacks.
items.rationale: Repeated attacks on ships crewed by Indians raise freight, insurance and crew-safety costs and keep oil supply risk high.

items.headline: Qatari mediators carry a revised US–Iran deal to Tehran; US president says the war will be 'wrapped up soon'
items.summary: Iran is expected to respond by the end of the week; sides still disagree on sequencing, with Tehran wanting the blockade and oil sanctions lifted first. An earlier draft was rejected. Diplomacy intensifying.
items.rationale: A deal reopening Hormuz would be the largest relief for India's oil bill, rupee and inflation, but failure raises strike risk after 3 November.

items.headline: Fiscal deficit widens 25.4% to ₹7.15 trillion in April–September, 42.1% of the full-year target
items.summary: Spending rose to ₹25.5 trillion from ₹23 trillion while net tax receipts grew only to ₹12.8 trillion. Higher food and fertiliser subsidies and subdued taxes drove it. New data; worsening.
items.rationale: Wider deficits raise the risk of more government borrowing, adding to pressure on G-Sec yields; subsidy costs rise with oil and gas prices.

items.headline: Forex reserves fall $1.27 billion to $719.75 billion, a seventh straight weekly decline
items.summary: Gold holdings fell $2.65 billion while foreign currency assets rose $1.36 billion. Reserves are about $66 billion below the September record. Ongoing but slowing.
items.rationale: Shrinking reserves limit the RBI's room to defend the rupee, though this week's drop was mostly gold valuation, not dollar sales.

items.headline: Rupee gains 33 paise to 94.93 per dollar on RBI intervention and softer crude
items.summary: It traded between 94.94 and 95.28; the dollar index slipped to 101.66. Biggest gain in weeks after holding near 95.3. Easing pressure.
items.rationale: A firmer rupee trims the cost of imported oil and inputs and supports foreign investor returns.

items.headline: 10-year G-Sec yield at 7.38%, down over 9 basis points on the week, ending a record 10-week losing run
items.summary: It had risen over 70 basis points in 10 weeks to 7.498% on Tuesday. Lower US yields after the Fed helped; some expect 7.70–7.75% by December. Easing for now.
items.rationale: Lower yields ease borrowing costs and bank bond losses, but high oil and a wider fiscal deficit could revive pressure.

items.headline: Global LNG prices jump 6%, raising gas costs as India imports record volumes
items.summary: Follows record October LNG imports for power, fertiliser and city gas, partly from Qatar. Escalating cost pressure.
items.rationale: Pricier LNG raises costs for gas-based power, fertiliser and city gas, adding to the subsidy bill and the trade deficit.
